question: Is the haze bad in Singapore today?
name: Claude
answer:
Yes, the haze looks bad. The latest reports I found are from 17 October 2026, and they show unhealthy air across Singapore. I can't see live data, so check the NEA site or the myENV app for current readings.

**Latest readings (17 Oct)**
- NEA's forecast for 17 Oct was a PSI of 150–230, which is Unhealthy to Very Unhealthy.
- At 2pm the 24-hour PSI was in the "unhealthy" range in all regions: central 184, north 135, south 154, east 173 and west 185.
- Central Singapore had been in the "very unhealthy" range the day before.
- At 2pm, hourly PM2.5 readings were 243 in the west, 179 in the central region, 162 in the south and 159 in the east.
- Afternoon showers kept hourly PM2.5 from climbing into the "very high" band.

**What to do**
- NEA advises healthy people to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion.
- The elderly, pregnant women, children and people with heart or lung conditions should limit time outdoors more strictly.
- Check the 1-hour PM2.5 reading before going outside. It changes faster than the 24-hour PSI.
- Wear an N95 mask if you have to be outdoors for long.

For live readings, see [NEA's haze page](https://www.nea.gov.sg) or [checkpointsg.com/haze](https://www.checkpointsg.com/haze).
